claims.text: The material is a PtPdRhRuIr high-entropy-alloy nanoparticle system.
Systematic control of composition ratio, nanoparticle size, and thermal annealing produces a homogeneous solid-solution phase.
The resulting solid solution has a controlled, uniform distribution of the noble-metal elements.
A uniform distribution of noble-metal elements causes synergistic enhancement of catalytic activity.
The catalytic enhancement arises from optimized adsorption and desorption of reactants and products.
The adsorption and desorption behavior is governed by the d-band-center mechanism.
Optimized PtPdRhRuIr nanoparticles will perform significantly better for CO oxidation than non-optimized nanoparticles.
Optimized PtPdRhRuIr nanoparticles will perform significantly better for the hydrogen evolution reaction than non-optimized nanoparticles.
Catalytic activity will reach a maximum at an optimal noble-metal composition ratio.
Catalytic activity will reach a maximum at an optimal nanoparticle size.
The proposed behavior is limited to optimized annealing conditions, particle sizes, and composition ratios.
Failure of the optimized nanoparticles to show a significant performance improvement over non-optimized nanoparticles would falsify the hypothesis.
